units.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 29, Biography 23

units.zh: 高祖三王
units.en: Three Princes of Gaozu
units.literal: Three Princes of Gaozu

units.zh: 高祖八男：丁貴嬪生昭明太子統，太宗簡文皇帝，廬陵威王續；
units.en: Emperor Wu of Liang had eight sons. Noble Consort Ding bore Crown Prince Zhaoming (Xiao Tong), Emperor Jianwen, and Prince Wei of Luling (Xiao Xu);
units.literal: Gaozu had eight sons: Noble Consort Ding bore Crown Prince Zhaoming (Tong), Emperor Jianwen of the Taizong line, and Prince Wei of Luling (Xu);

units.zh: 阮脩容生世祖孝元皇帝；
units.en: Lady Ruan Xiurong bore Emperor Yuan (Xiao Yi);
units.literal: Lady Ruan Xiurong bore Emperor Yuan (Xiao Yi) of the Shizu line;

units.zh: 吳淑媛生豫章王綜；
units.en: Lady Wu Shuyuan bore the Prince of Yuzhang (Xiao Zong);
units.literal: Lady Wu Shuyuan bore Prince of Yuzhang (Zong);

units.zh: 董淑儀生南康簡王績；
units.en: Lady Dong Shuyi bore Prince Jian of Nankang (Xiao Ji);
units.literal: Lady Dong Shuyi bore Prince Jian of Nankang (Ji);

units.zh: 丁充華生邵陵攜王綸；
units.en: Lady Ding Chonghua bore Prince Xie of Shaoling (Xiao Lun);
units.literal: Lady Ding Chonghua bore Prince Xie of Shaoling (Lun);

units.zh: 葛脩容生武陵王紀。
units.en: Lady Ge Xiurong bore the Prince of Wuling (Xiao Ji).
units.literal: Lady Ge Xiurong bore Prince of Wuling (Ji).

units.zh: 綜及紀別有傳。
units.en: Zong and Ji are treated in separate biographies.
units.literal: Zong and Ji have separate biographies.

units.zh: 南康簡王績字世謹，高祖第四子。
units.en: Prince Jian of Nankang, Xiao Ji, styled Shijin, was Emperor Wu's fourth son.
units.literal: Prince Jian of Nankang, Ji, styled Shijin, was the fourth son of Gaozu.

units.zh: 天監八年，封南康郡王，邑二千戶。
units.en: In 509, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nankang with a fief of two thousand households.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Tianjian, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nankang commandery with a fief of two thousand households.

units.zh: 出爲輕車將軍，領石頭戍軍事。
units.en: He was appointed General of Light Chariots and placed in command of the Shitou garrison.
units.literal: He went out to serve as General of Light Chariots and concurrently held command of the Shitou garrison.

units.zh: 十年，遷使持節、都督南徐州諸軍事、南徐州刺史，進號仁威將軍。
units.en: In 511, he was made Bearer of the Staff, commander of South Xuzhou forces, and regional inspector of South Xuzhou, with the additional title General of Benevolent Might.
units.literal: In the tenth year, he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander over all military affairs of South Xuzhou, and Regional Inspector of South Xuzhou, and advanced in title to General of Benevolent Might.

units.zh: 績時年七歲，主者有受貨，洗改解書，長史王僧孺弗之覺，績見而輒詰之，便卽時首服，衆咸歎其聰警。
units.en: Ji was only seven. A clerk had taken a bribe and altered an imperial rescript by washing and rewriting the text. Chief Administrator Wang Sengru had not noticed, but Ji spotted the fraud and questioned it on the spot; the clerk confessed immediately, and everyone marveled at his sharp mind.
units.literal: Ji was then seven years old. A clerk had taken a bribe and altered an imperial rescript by washing and rewriting it. Chief Administrator Wang Sengru did not detect it, but when Ji saw it he at once questioned the matter, and the man immediately confessed. All marveled at his keen intelligence.

units.zh: 十六年，徵爲宣毅將軍、領石頭戍軍事。
units.en: In 517, he was recalled to serve as General Who Proclaims Martial Resolution and again took command of the Shitou garrison.
units.literal: In the sixteenth year, he was summoned as General Who Proclaims Martial Resolution and concurrently held command of the Shitou garrison.

units.zh: 十七年，出爲使持節、都督南北兗徐青冀五州諸軍事、南兗州刺史，在州著稱。
units.en: In 518, he was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, commander of forces in North and South Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, and regional inspector of South Yanzhou, where he earned a strong reputation.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year, he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs of the five provinces of North and South Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, and Regional Inspector of South Yanzhou, and won a distinguished reputation in the province.

units.zh: 尋有詔徵還，民曹嘉樂等三百七十人詣闕上表，稱績尤異一十五條，乞留州任，優詔許之，進號北中郎將。
units.en: He was soon recalled by edict, but Jia Le of the Bureau of the People and three hundred seventy others went to the capital and submitted a memorial listing fifteen exceptional deeds of Ji and asking that he remain in office. The emperor granted their request with a gracious edict and promoted him to General of the North Central Commandant.
units.literal: Soon an edict summoned him back to court. Jia Le of the Bureau of the People and three hundred seventy others went to the capital and submitted a memorial listing fifteen outstanding merits of Ji and begging that he be kept in his provincial post. An excellent edict granted this, and he was advanced in title to General of the North Central Commandant.

units.zh: 普通四年，徵爲侍中、雲麾將軍，領石頭戍軍事。
units.en: In 523, he was recalled as palace attendant and General of the Cloud Pennant, with concurrent command of the Shitou garrison.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Putong, he was summoned as Palace Attendant and General of the Cloud Pennant, and concurrently held command of the Shitou garrison.

units.zh: 五年，出爲使持節、都督江州諸軍事、江州刺史。
units.en: In 524, he was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, commander of Jiangzhou forces, and regional inspector of Jiangzhou.
units.literal: In the fifth year, he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs of Jiangzhou, and Regional Inspector of Jiangzhou.

units.zh: 丁董淑儀憂，居喪過禮，高祖手詔勉之，使攝州任，固求解職，乃徵授安右將軍、領石頭戍軍事，尋加護軍。
units.en: When Lady Dong Shuyi died, he mourned her beyond the prescribed rites. Emperor Wu wrote to him in his own hand urging restraint and had him continue to administer the province, but Ji insisted on resigning. He was then recalled as General Who Pacifies the Right with command of the Shitou garrison and soon made Protector of the Army as well.
units.literal: He entered mourning for Lady Dong Shuyi and observed the rites beyond what was prescribed. Gaozu personally wrote an edict to encourage him and had him act in the provincial post, but he firmly sought to resign his duties. He was then summoned and appointed General Who Pacifies the Right and given command of the Shitou garrison, and soon after was made added Protector of the Army.

units.zh: 羸瘠弗堪視事。
units.en: Wasted by grief, he was unable to carry out his duties.
units.literal: Emaciated and wasted, he could not bear to attend to his duties.

units.zh: 大通三年，因感病薨于任，時年二十五。
units.en: In 531, he died in office of an illness brought on by mourning, at the age of twenty-five.
units.literal: In the third year of Datong, he died in office from an illness contracted in mourning, at age twenty-five.

units.zh: 贈侍中、中軍將軍、開府儀同三司，給鼓吹一部。
units.en: He was posthumously honored as palace attendant, General of the Central Army, and Grand Master with an establishment equal to the Three Excellencies, and granted one set of martial music.
units.literal: Posthumously he was given Palace Attendant, General of the Central Army, and the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies with an establishment, and one set of martial music was granted.

units.zh: 諡曰簡。
units.en: His posthumous title was Jian (Plain).
units.literal: His posthumous title was Jian.

units.zh: 績寡玩好，少嗜欲，居無僕妾，躬事約儉，所有租秩，悉寄天府。
units.en: Ji cared little for amusements and had few wants. He kept no servants or concubines, lived frugally with his own hands, and sent all his income and stipends to the imperial treasury.
units.literal: Ji had few diversions and little desire; he kept no servants or concubines, personally practiced frugality, and sent all his rent and salary to the imperial treasury.

units.zh: 及薨後，府有南康國無名錢數千萬。
units.en: After his death, the Nankang princely establishment was found to hold several tens of millions in unrecorded cash.
units.literal: After his death, the princely establishment of Nankang held several tens of millions in unaccounted cash.

units.zh: 子會理嗣，字長才。
units.en: His son Huili succeeded him; Huili's style was Changcai.
units.literal: His son Huili succeeded him, styled Changcai.

units.zh: 少聰慧，好文史。
units.en: As a youth he was clever and devoted to literature and history.
units.literal: In youth he was clever and fond of literature and history.

units.zh: 年十一而孤，特爲高祖所愛，衣服禮秩與正王不殊。
units.en: Orphaned at eleven, he was especially favored by Emperor Wu, and his dress and ceremonial standing were no different from those of a full prince.
units.literal: Orphaned at eleven, he was especially loved by Gaozu; his clothing and ceremonial rank were no different from those of a full prince.

units.zh: 年十五，拜輕車將軍、湘州刺史，又領石頭戍軍事。
units.en: At fifteen he was made General of Light Chariots and regional inspector of Xiangzhou, and again took command of the Shitou garrison.
units.literal: At fifteen he was appointed General of Light Chariots and Regional Inspector of Xiangzhou, and again held command of the Shitou garrison.

units.zh: 遷侍中，兼領軍將軍。
units.en: He was promoted to palace attendant and concurrently made General Who Leads the Army.
units.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant and concurrently made General Who Leads the Army.

units.zh: 尋除宣惠將軍、丹陽尹，置佐史。
units.en: He was soon appointed General Who Proclaims Grace and governor of Danyang, with a full staff.
units.literal: Soon he was made General Who Proclaims Grace and Governor of Danyang, with staff officers appointed.

units.zh: 出爲使持節、都督南北兗北徐青冀東徐譙七州諸軍事、平北將軍、南兗州刺史。
units.en: He was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, commander of forces in seven provinces—North and South Yan, North Xu, Qing, Ji, East Xu, and Qiao—as General Who Pacifies the North and regional inspector of South Yanzhou.
units.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs of the seven provinces of North and South Yan, North Xu, Qing, Ji, East Xu, and Qiao, General Who Pacifies the North, and Regional Inspector of South Yanzhou.

units.zh: 太清元年，督衆軍北討，至彭城，爲魏師所敗，退歸本鎮。
units.en: In 547, he led the armies on a northern campaign. At Pengcheng he was defeated by Northern Wei troops and retreated to his headquarters.
units.literal: In the first year of Taiqing, he directed the armies on a northern campaign. Reaching Pengcheng, he was defeated by Wei forces and withdrew to his base command.

units.zh: 二年，侯景圍京邑，會理治嚴將入援，會北徐州刺史封山侯正表將應其兄正德，外託赴援，實謀襲廣陵，會理擊破之。
units.en: In 548, Hou Jing besieged the capital. Huili prepared his troops to march to the relief of the court. Meanwhile Marquis Zhengbiao of Fengshan, regional inspector of North Xuzhou, was about to join his elder brother Zhengde. He claimed to be coming to help, but in fact planned to seize Guangling. Huili routed him.
units.literal: In the second year, Hou Jing besieged the capital. Huili made his troops ready to enter in relief. At that time Fengshan Marquis Zhengbiao, Regional Inspector of North Xuzhou, was about to join his elder brother Zhengde. Outwardly he claimed to come to the rescue, but in fact he plotted to strike Guangling. Huili defeated him.

units.zh: 方得進路，臺城陷，侯景遣前臨江太守董紹先以高祖手敕召會理，其僚佐咸勸距之。
units.en: He had barely secured his line of advance when the imperial city fell. Hou Jing sent the former administrator of Linjiang, Dong Shaoxian, to summon Huili with a personal edict in Emperor Wu's hand. His officers all urged him to refuse.
units.literal: He had just cleared his route forward when Taicheng fell. Hou Jing sent the former Administrator of Linjiang, Dong Shaoxian, to summon Huili with a personal edict in Gaozu's hand. All his staff urged him to refuse.

units.zh: 會理曰：「諸君心事，與我不同，天子年尊，受制賊虜，今有手敕召我入朝，臣子之心，豈得違背。
units.en: Huili said, "Your intentions are not mine. The emperor is old and in the rebels' power. Now I have his own edict summoning me to court. How could a loyal subject refuse?
units.literal: Huili said, "Your hearts are not the same as mine. The Son of Heaven is advanced in years and held captive by the bandit. Now there is a personal edict summoning me to court. How could the heart of a subject disobey?

units.zh: 且遠處江北，功業難成，不若身赴京都，圖之肘腋。
units.en: Besides, holding the far north of the Yangzi, we can accomplish little. Better to go to the capital myself and strike from within.
units.literal: Moreover, stationed far away north of the river, it would be hard to achieve great deeds. It is better to go in person to the capital and plot from close at hand.

units.zh: 吾計決矣。」
units.en: My mind is made up."
units.literal: My decision is made."

units.zh: 遂席捲而行，以城輸紹先。
units.en: He then marched off with all his forces and handed the city over to Shaoxian.
units.literal: He then swept away with all his forces and surrendered the city to Shaoxian.

units.zh: 至京，景以爲侍中、司空、兼中書令。
units.en: When he reached the capital, Hou Jing appointed him palace attendant, Minister of Works, and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: On reaching the capital, Jing made him Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 雖在寇手，每思匡復，與西鄉侯勸等潛布腹心，要結壯士。
units.en: Though held by the rebels, he constantly plotted restoration. With Marquis Qu of Western Township and others he secretly placed agents and rallied stalwart men.
units.literal: Though in the enemy's hands, he constantly thought of restoring the realm. With Western Township Marquis Qu and others he secretly placed trusted men and bound brave warriors to the cause.

units.zh: 時范陽祖皓斬紹先，據廣陵城起義，期以會理爲內應。
units.en: At that time Zu Hao of Fanyang killed Shaoxian, seized Guangling, and rose in revolt, planning for Huili to act as his contact inside the capital.
units.literal: At that time Zu Hao of Fanyang killed Shaoxian, seized Guangling city, and rose in revolt, setting a date with Huili as the inside contact.

units.zh: 皓敗，辭相連及，景矯詔免會理官，猶以白衣領尚書令。
units.en: When Hao was defeated, testimony implicated Huili. Hou Jing forged an edict stripping him of rank, yet still had him, as a commoner in dress, serve as head of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: When Hao was defeated, testimony implicated Huili. Jing forged an edict removing Huili from office, yet still had him, in plain dress, head the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 是冬，景往晉熙，景師虛弱，會理復與柳敬禮謀之。
units.en: That winter Hou Jing went to Jinxi. His garrison was weak, and Huili again plotted with Liu Jingli.
units.literal: That winter Jing went to Jinxi. His forces were thin, and Huili again plotted with Liu Jingli.

units.zh: 敬禮曰：「舉大事必有所資，今無寸兵，安可以動？」
units.en: Jingli said, "A great undertaking needs resources. We have not a single soldier. How can we act?"
units.literal: Jingli said, "To undertake a great affair one must have resources. Now we have not a single soldier. How can we move?"

units.zh: 會理曰：「湖熟有吾舊兵三千餘人，昨來相知，克期響集，聽吾日定，便至京師。
units.en: Huili said, "At Hushu I still have more than three thousand of my old troops. I contacted them yesterday; they will rally on the day I set. Give me a date, and I will come to the capital at once.
units.literal: Huili said, "At Hushu I have more than three thousand of my old troops. Yesterday I made contact with them; they will gather on the appointed day. Hear me set the day, and I will come straight to the capital.

units.zh: 計賊守兵不過千人耳，若大兵外攻，吾等內應，直取王偉，事必有成。
units.en: The rebel garrison cannot be more than a thousand. If a main force attacks from outside while we rise within and seize Wang Wei directly, we are sure to succeed.
units.literal: I reckon the rebel garrison is no more than a thousand men. If a great army attacks from outside and we respond from within, striking straight at Wang Wei, the affair is sure to succeed.

units.zh: 縱景後歸，無能爲也。」
units.en: Even if Hou Jing returns afterward, he will be powerless."
units.literal: Even if Jing returns later, he will be unable to act."

units.zh: 敬禮曰「善」，因贊成之。
units.en: Jingli said, "Good," and backed the plan.
units.literal: Jingli said, "Good," and thereupon endorsed the plan.

units.zh: 于時百姓厭賊，咸思用命，自丹陽至于京口，靡不同之。
units.en: The people were sick of the rebels and eager to fight. From Danyang to Jingkou, everyone felt the same.
units.literal: At that time the people were weary of the bandits and all wished to give their lives. From Danyang to Jingkou, none differed in this.

units.zh: 後事不果，與弟祁陽侯通理並遇害。
units.en: The plot failed in the end, and he and his younger brother, Marquis Tongli of Qiyang, were both killed.
units.literal: Later the affair did not succeed, and he and his younger brother, Qiyang Marquis Tongli, were both killed.

units.zh: 通理字仲宣，位太子洗馬，封祁陽侯。
units.en: Tongli, styled Zhongxuan, served as groom in the heir apparent's household and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qiyang.
units.literal: Tongli, styled Zhongxuan, held the post of Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qiyang.

units.zh: 通理弟乂理字季英，會理第六弟也。
units.en: Tongli's younger brother Yili, styled Jiying, was Huili's sixth brother.
units.literal: Tongli's younger brother Yili, styled Jiying, was Huili's sixth younger brother.

units.zh: 生十旬而簡王薨，至三歲而能言，見內人分散，涕泣相送，乂理問其故，或曰：「此簡王宮人，喪畢去爾。」
units.en: He was only a hundred days old when Prince Jian died. By three he could speak. When he saw palace women being sent away, weeping as they parted, Yili asked why. Someone said, "These were Prince Jian's women. Now that mourning is over, they are leaving."
units.literal: When he had lived a hundred days, Prince Jian died; by three he could speak. Seeing palace women being dispersed, weeping and seeing one another off, Yili asked the reason. Someone said, "These are the palace women of Prince Jian. When mourning is finished they will leave."

units.zh: 乂理便號泣，悲不自勝，諸宮人見之，莫不傷感，爲之停者三人焉。
units.en: Yili burst into wailing he could not control. The palace women were all moved, and three of them stayed because of him.
units.literal: Yili at once wailed aloud, grief beyond bearing. The palace women who saw it were all moved to sorrow, and three of them stayed on his account.

units.zh: 服闋後，見高祖，又悲泣不自勝。
units.en: After mourning ended, when he saw Emperor Wu, he wept again until he could not control himself.
units.literal: After mourning ended, when he saw Gaozu, he again wept in grief beyond bearing.

units.zh: 高祖爲之流涕，謂左右曰：「此兒大必爲奇士。」
units.en: Emperor Wu wept as well and told his attendants, "When this boy grows up, he will surely be a remarkable man."
units.literal: Gaozu wept for him and said to those at his side, "When this boy grows up he will surely be an extraordinary man."

units.zh: 大同八年，封安樂縣侯，邑五百戶。
units.en: In 542, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anle with a fief of five hundred households.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Datong, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anle county with a fief of five hundred households.

units.zh: 乂理性慷慨，慕立功名，每讀書見忠臣烈士，未嘗不廢卷歎曰：「一生之內，當無愧古人。」
units.en: Yili was ardent by nature and longed to win fame. Whenever he read of loyal ministers and martyrs, he would set the book down and sigh, "In one lifetime a man ought not to be ashamed before the ancients."
units.literal: Yili was by nature generous and ardent, aspiring to establish merit and fame. Whenever in reading he came upon loyal ministers and martyrs, he never failed to lay down the scroll and sigh, "Within one lifetime one ought not to be ashamed before the ancients."

units.zh: 博覽多識，有文才，嘗祭孔文舉墓，幷爲立碑，制文甚美。
units.en: He read widely and knew much, and had literary talent. He once sacrificed at the tomb of Kong Rong and erected a stele for him; the inscription he composed was excellent.
units.literal: Broad in reading and rich in knowledge, he had literary talent. Once he sacrificed at the tomb of Kong Wenju and also erected a stele for him; the composition was very fine.

units.zh: 太清中，侯景內寇，乂理聚賓客數百，輕裝赴南兗州，隨兄會理入援，恒親當矢石，爲士卒先。
units.en: During the Taiqing era, when Hou Jing invaded the interior, Yili gathered several hundred retainers, went lightly equipped to South Yanzhou, and followed his brother Huili to relieve the capital. He always placed himself in the line of fire ahead of his men.
units.literal: In the Taiqing era, when Hou Jing invaded within the realm, Yili gathered several hundred guests, went in light equipment to South Yanzhou, and followed his elder brother Huili in entering to relieve the capital. He always personally faced arrows and stones and went before the soldiers.

units.zh: 及城陷，又隨會理還廣陵，因入齊爲質，乞師。
units.en: When the capital fell, he followed Huili back to Guangling, then went to Northern Qi as a hostage to beg for troops.
units.literal: When the city fell, he again followed Huili back to Guangling, then entered Qi as a hostage to beg for troops.

units.zh: 行二日，會侯景遣董紹先據廣陵，遂追會理，因爲所獲。
units.en: Two days into the journey, Hou Jing sent Dong Shaoxian to seize Guangling. Shaoxian then pursued Huili, and Yili was captured.
units.literal: After two days on the road, it happened that Hou Jing sent Dong Shaoxian to seize Guangling. Shaoxian then pursued Huili, and Yili was captured.

units.zh: 紹先防之甚嚴，不得與兄弟相見，乃偽請先還京，得入辭母，謂其姊安固公主曰：「事旣如此，豈可闔家受斃。
units.en: Shaoxian guarded him closely and would not let him see his brothers. Yili pretended to ask to return to the capital first. Allowed to bid farewell to his mother, he told his elder sister, Princess Angu, "Matters being what they are, the whole family cannot simply be killed together.
units.literal: Shaoxian guarded him very strictly and would not let him see his brothers. He then falsely asked to return to the capital first. Allowed to enter and take leave of his mother, he said to his elder sister, Princess Angu, "Since matters have come to this, how can the whole family be slaughtered together?

units.zh: 兄若至，願爲言之，善爲計自勉，勿賜以爲念也。
units.en: If our elder brother comes, please tell him. Make good plans for yourselves and take heart. Do not worry about me.
units.literal: If my elder brother arrives, I beg you speak for me. Take good thought for your own plans and encourage yourselves. Do not grieve on my account.

units.zh: 家國阽危，雖死非恨，前途亦思立效，但未知天命何如耳！」
units.en: The state and our house are in peril. I do not regret death, and I still hope to serve ahead—but who knows what fate will allow!"
units.literal: The state and the family stand on the brink of peril. Though I die, I have no regret. I also intend to achieve merit ahead, but I do not know what Heaven's mandate will be!"

units.zh: 至京師，以魏降人元貞立節忠正，可以託孤，乃以玉柄扇贈之。
units.en: In the capital he judged the Northern Wei defector Yuan Zhen upright and trustworthy enough to entrust with a final charge, and gave him a fan with a jade handle.
units.literal: On reaching the capital, he took the Wei defector Yuan Zhen to be upright in integrity and fit to receive a deathbed charge, and gave him a fan with a jade handle.

units.zh: 貞怪其故，不受。
units.en: Zhen wondered at this and refused the gift.
units.literal: Zhen wondered at the reason and would not accept.

units.zh: 乂理曰：「後當見憶，幸勿推辭。」
units.en: Yili said, "You will remember me later. Please do not refuse."
units.literal: Yili said, "Later you will remember me. I beg you not to decline."

units.zh: 會祖皓起兵，乂理奔長蘆，收軍得千餘人。
units.en: When Zu Hao rose in revolt, Yili fled to Changlu and raised more than a thousand men.
units.literal: When Zu Hao rose in arms, Yili fled to Changlu and gathered troops, obtaining more than a thousand men.

units.zh: 其左右有應賊者，因間劫會理，其衆遂駭散，爲景所害，時年二十一。
units.en: Some of his followers sided with the rebels. They seized an opening to kidnap Huili; Yili's force panicked and scattered, and Hou Jing killed him. He was twenty-one.
units.literal: Among those at his side were some who sided with the bandits. Taking advantage of an opening, they seized Huili. His force was then thrown into panic and scattered, and he was killed by Jing at age twenty-one.

units.zh: 元貞始悟其前言，往收葬焉。
units.en: Yuan Zhen then understood what he had meant earlier and went to recover and bury him.
units.literal: Yuan Zhen then understood his earlier words and went to gather and bury him.

units.zh: 廬陵威王續字世䐶，高祖第五子，天監八年，封廬陵郡王，邑二千戶。
units.en: Prince Wei of Luling, Xiao Xu, styled Shiyin, was Emperor Wu's fifth son. In 509 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Luling with a fief of two thousand households.
units.literal: Prince Wei of Luling, Xu, styled Shiyin, was the fifth son of Gaozu. In the eighth year of Tianjian he was enfeoffed as Prince of Luling commandery with a fief of two thousand households.

units.zh: 十年，拜輕車將軍、南彭城琅邪太守。
units.en: In 511 he was made General of Light Chariots and administrator of Nan Pengcheng and Langye.
units.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed General of Light Chariots and Administrator of Nan Pengcheng and Langye.

units.zh: 十三年，轉會稽太守。
units.en: In 514 he was transferred to administrator of Kuaiji.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Administrator of Kuaiji.

units.zh: 十六年，爲都督江州諸軍事、雲麾將軍、江州刺史。
units.en: In 517 he was made commander of Jiangzhou forces, General of the Cloud Pennant, and regional inspector of Jiangzhou.
units.literal: In the sixteenth year he became Commander over military affairs of Jiangzhou, General of the Cloud Pennant, and Regional Inspector of Jiangzhou.

units.zh: 普通元年，徵爲宣毅將軍，領石頭戍軍事。
units.en: In 520 he was recalled as General Who Proclaims Martial Resolution with command of the Shitou garrison.
units.literal: In the first year of Putong he was summoned as General Who Proclaims Martial Resolution and held command of the Shitou garrison.

units.zh: 續少英果，膂力絕人，馳射游獵，應發命中。
units.en: As a youth Xu was bold and resolute, with extraordinary strength. In mounted archery and the hunt, every shot he loosed found its mark.
units.literal: Xu in youth was brave and resolute, with strength beyond other men. In mounted archery and hunting, every shot he loosed struck home.

units.zh: 高祖常歎曰：「此我之任城也。」
units.en: Emperor Wu often exclaimed, "He is my Rencheng!"
units.literal: Gaozu often sighed and said, "This is my Rencheng."

units.zh: 嘗與臨賀王正德及胡貴通、趙伯超等馳射于高祖前，續冠于諸人，高祖大悅。
units.en: Once he competed in mounted archery before Emperor Wu with Prince Zhengde of Linhe, Hu Guitong, Zhao Bochao, and others. Xu outshot them all, and the emperor was delighted.
units.literal: Once he rode and shot before Gaozu together with Prince of Linhe Zhengde and Hu Guitong, Zhao Bochao, and others. Xu took first place among them all, and Gaozu was greatly pleased.

units.zh: 三年，爲使持節、都督雍、梁、秦、沙四州諸軍事、西中郎將、雍州刺史。
units.en: In 522 he was made Bearer of the Staff, commander of forces in Yong, Liang, Qin, and Sha, General of the West Central Commandant, and regional inspector of Yongzhou.
units.literal: In the third year he became Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs of the four provinces of Yong, Liang, Qin, and Sha, General of the West Central Commandant, and Regional Inspector of Yongzhou.

units.zh: 七年，加宣毅將軍。
units.en: In 526 he was given the additional title General Who Proclaims Martial Resolution.
units.literal: In the seventh year he was given the additional title General Who Proclaims Martial Resolution.

units.zh: 中大通二年，又爲使持節、都督雍、梁、秦、沙四州諸軍事、平北將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史，給鼓吹一部。
units.en: In 530 he again became Bearer of the Staff, commander of Yong, Liang, Qin, and Sha, General Who Pacifies the North, Colonel Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and regional inspector of Yongzhou, with one set of martial music granted.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhongdatong he again became Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs of the four provinces of Yong, Liang, Qin, and Sha, General Who Pacifies the North, Colonel Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and Regional Inspector of Yongzhou, and one set of martial music was granted.

units.zh: 續多聚馬仗，畜養驍雄，金帛內盈，倉廩外實。
units.en: Xu stockpiled horses and arms, raised fierce fighters, and filled his treasuries and granaries to overflowing.
units.literal: Xu amassed many horses and weapons, raised fierce champions, filled his inner stores with gold and silk, and made his outer granaries solid.

units.zh: 四年，遷安北將軍。
units.en: In 532 he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North.

units.zh: 大同元年，爲使持節、都督江州諸軍事、安南將軍、江州刺史。
units.en: In 535 he was made Bearer of the Staff, commander of Jiangzhou forces, General Who Pacifies the South, and regional inspector of Jiangzhou.
units.literal: In the first year of Datong he became Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs of Jiangzhou, General Who Pacifies the South, and Regional Inspector of Jiangzhou.

units.zh: 三年，徵爲護軍將軍、領石頭戍軍事。
units.en: In 537 he was recalled as Protector of the Army with command of the Shitou garrison.
units.literal: In the third year he was summoned as Protector of the Army and held command of the Shitou garrison.

units.zh: 五年，爲驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司。
units.en: In 539 he was made General of Agile Cavalry with an establishment equal to the Three Excellencies.
units.literal: In the fifth year he became General of Agile Cavalry and was given the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies with an establishment.

units.zh: 又出爲使持節、都督荊郢司雍南北秦梁巴華九州諸軍事、荊州刺史。
units.en: He was again sent out as Bearer of the Staff, commander of forces in nine provinces—Jing, Ying, Si, Yong, North and South Qin, Liang, Ba, and Hua—and regional inspector of Jingzhou.
units.literal: He again went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs of the nine provinces of Jing, Ying, Si, Yong, North and South Qin, Liang, Ba, and Hua, and Regional Inspector of Jingzhou.

units.zh: 中大同二年，薨於州，時年四十四。
units.en: In 546 he died in office at the age of forty-four.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhong Datong he died in the province at age forty-four.

units.zh: 贈司空、散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍，鼓吹一部，諡曰威。
units.en: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Works, regular attendant, and Grand General of Agile Cavalry, with one set of martial music. His posthumous title was Wei (Martial).
units.literal: Posthumously he was given Minister of Works, Regular Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat, and Grand General of Agile Cavalry, with one set of martial music. His posthumous title was Wei.

units.zh: 長子安嗣。
units.en: His eldest son was Ansi.
units.literal: His eldest son was Ansi.

units.zh: 邵陵攜王綸字世調，高祖第六子也。
units.en: Prince Xie of Shaoling, Xiao Lun, styled Shitiao, was Emperor Wu's sixth son.
units.literal: Prince Xie of Shaoling, Lun, styled Shitiao, was the sixth son of Gaozu.

units.zh: 少聰穎，博學善屬文，尤工尺牘。
units.en: As a youth he was clever and widely learned, skilled at composition and especially at letter-writing.
units.literal: In youth he was clever and quick, broadly learned and skilled at composition, especially adept at letters.

units.zh: 天監十三年，封邵陵郡王，邑二千戶。
units.en: In 514 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shaoling with a fief of two thousand households.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianjian he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shaoling commandery with a fief of two thousand households.

units.zh: 出爲寧遠將軍、琅邪、彭城二郡太守，遷輕車將軍、會稽太守。
units.en: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the Distant and administrator of Langye and Pengcheng, then promoted to General of Light Chariots and administrator of Kuaiji.
units.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the Distant, Administrator of the two commanderies of Langye and Pengcheng, and was transferred to General of Light Chariots and Administrator of Kuaiji.

units.zh: 十八年，徵爲信威將軍。
units.en: In 519 he was recalled as General of Trustworthy Might.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year he was summoned as General of Trustworthy Might.

units.zh: 普通元年，領石頭戍軍事，尋爲江州刺史。
units.en: In 520 he took command of the Shitou garrison and soon became regional inspector of Jiangzhou.
units.literal: In the first year of Putong he held command of the Shitou garrison, and soon became Regional Inspector of Jiangzhou.

units.zh: 五年，以西中郎將權攝南兗州，坐事免官奪爵。
units.en: In 524, serving as General of the West Central Commandant, he acted as regent of South Yanzhou. For an offense he was dismissed and stripped of his title.
units.literal: In the fifth year, as General of the West Central Commandant he acted in place as regent of South Yanzhou. Because of an offense he was dismissed from office and stripped of his rank.

units.zh: 七年，拜侍中。
units.en: In 526 he was appointed attendant-in-ordinary.
units.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 大通元年，復封爵，尋加信威將軍，置佐史。
units.en: In 527 his title was restored; soon after he was made General of Trustworthy Might, with adjutants and clerks assigned.
units.literal: In the first year of Datong (AD 527) his title was restored; soon afterward he was additionally made General of Trustworthy Might, with adjutants and clerks appointed.

units.zh: 中大通元年，爲丹陽尹。
units.en: In 529 he became intendant of Danyang.
units.literal: In the first year of Zhongdatong he became Intendant of Danyang.

units.zh: 四年，爲侍中、宣惠將軍、揚州刺史。
units.en: In 532 he was appointed attendant-in-ordinary, General Who Promotes Grace, and regional inspector of Yangzhou.
units.literal: In the fourth year he served as Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Promotes Grace, and Regional Inspector of Yangzhou.

units.zh: 以侵漁細民，少府丞何智通以事啓聞，綸知之，令客戴子高於都巷刺殺之。
units.en: Because he had preyed on the common people, Vice Director of the Privy Treasury He Zhitong reported him to the throne. Xiao Lun learned of it and had his retainer Dai Zigao stab him to death in a city alley.
units.literal: For exploiting and extorting the common people, Vice Director of the Privy Treasury He Zhitong reported the matter to the throne. When Xiao Lun learned of it, he had his retainer Dai Zigao assassinate him in a capital lane.

units.zh: 智通子訴于闕下，高祖令圍綸第，捕子高，綸匿之，竟不出。
units.en: He Zhitong's son appealed at the palace gates. Emperor Wu ordered Xiao Lun's residence surrounded and Dai Zigao arrested. Xiao Lun hid him and refused to hand him over.
units.literal: He Zhitong's son appealed at the palace gates. Emperor Wu ordered Xiao Lun's residence surrounded and Dai Zigao seized. Xiao Lun hid him and would not surrender him.

units.zh: 坐免爲庶人。
units.en: He was stripped of office and reduced to commoner status.
units.literal: He was punished by dismissal and reduction to commoner status.

units.zh: 頃之，復封爵。
units.en: Before long his title was restored.
units.literal: Before long his title was restored.

units.zh: 大同元年，爲侍中、雲麾將軍。
units.en: In 535 he was appointed attendant-in-ordinary and General of Cloudy Pennants.
units.literal: In the first year of Datong he was Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Cloudy Pennants.

units.zh: 七年，出爲使持節、都督郢定霍司四州諸軍事、平西將軍、郢州刺史，遷爲安前將軍、丹陽尹。
units.en: In 541 he was sent out with imperial credentials as area commander over Ying, Ding, Huo, and Si provinces, as General Who Pacifies the West and regional inspector of Yingzhou, then transferred to General Who Secures the Vanguard and intendant of Danyang.
units.literal: In the seventh year he went out as bearer of the staff of authority, Area Commander of military affairs in the four provinces of Ying, Ding, Huo, and Si, General Who Pacifies the West, and Regional Inspector of Yingzhou; he was transferred to General Who Secures the Vanguard and Intendant of Danyang.

units.zh: 中大同元年，出爲鎮東將軍、南徐州刺史。
units.en: In 546 he was appointed General Who Guards the East and regional inspector of South Xuzhou.
units.literal: In the first year of Zhong Datong he went out as General Who Guards the East and Regional Inspector of South Xuzhou.

units.zh: 太清二年，進位中衛將軍、開府儀同三司。
units.en: In 548 he was promoted to General of the Central Guard with an honorific suite equal to the Three Departments.
units.literal: In the second year of Taiqing he was promoted to General of the Central Guard with the privilege of an office equal to a three-department suite.

units.zh: 侯景構逆，加征討大都督，率衆討景。
units.en: When Hou Jing plotted rebellion, Xiao Lun was additionally made grand area commander to campaign and punish, and he led an army against Hou Jing.
units.literal: When Hou Jing plotted rebellion, the additional post of Grand Area Commander to Campaign and Punish was conferred on him, and he led troops to attack Hou Jing.

units.zh: 將發，高祖誡曰：「侯景小豎，頗習行陣，未可以一戰卽殄，當以歲月圖之。」
units.en: As he was about to set out, Emperor Wu warned him: "Hou Jing is a petty rebel who knows his way around a battlefield. You cannot wipe him out in one battle—you must wear him down over time."
units.literal: As he was about to depart, Emperor Wu admonished him, saying: "Hou Jing is a petty upstart who is well practiced in battle formations; he cannot be destroyed in a single engagement—you must plan to take him over months."

units.zh: 綸次鐘離，景已度釆石。
units.en: By the time Xiao Lun reached Zhongli, Hou Jing had already crossed Caishi.
units.literal: When Xiao Lun was camped at Zhongli, Hou Jing had already crossed Caishi.

units.zh: 綸乃晝夜兼道，遊軍入赴。
units.en: Xiao Lun then forced day-and-night marches, sending advance units to rush to the relief.
units.literal: Xiao Lun then marched day and night by forced stages; advance detachments entered to relieve the capital.

units.zh: 濟江中流，風起，人馬溺者十一二。
units.en: Crossing the Yangzi midstream, a wind sprang up and one or two men and horses in ten were drowned.
units.literal: As they crossed the Yangzi midstream, wind arose, and one or two out of ten men and horses drowned.

units.zh: 遂率寧遠將軍西豊公大春、新淦公大成等，步騎三萬，發自京口。
units.en: He then led General Who Pacifies the Distance Duke of Xifeng Dachun, Duke of Xingan Dacheng, and others—thirty thousand foot and horse—setting out from Jingkou.
units.literal: Thereupon he led General Who Pacifies the Distance Duke of Xifeng Dachun, Duke of Xingan Dacheng, and others—thirty thousand infantry and cavalry—setting out from Jingkou.

units.zh: 將軍趙伯超曰：「若從黃城大道，必與賊遇，不如徑路直指鐘山，出其不意。」
units.en: General Zhao Bochao said: "If we take the Huangcheng highway we are sure to run into the rebels. Better to strike straight for Zhongshan by a direct route and take them by surprise."
units.literal: General Zhao Bochao said: "If we take the Huangcheng main road, we are certain to encounter the rebels; it would be better to take a direct route straight for Zhongshan and catch them unawares."

units.zh: 綸從之。
units.en: Xiao Lun agreed.
units.literal: Xiao Lun followed his advice.

units.zh: 衆軍奄至，賊徒大駭，分爲三道攻綸，綸與戰，大破之，斬首千餘級。
units.en: The army arrived without warning. The rebels were terrified, split into three columns, and attacked Xiao Lun. He fought them and won a great victory, taking more than a thousand heads.
units.literal: The army suddenly arrived. The rebel troops were greatly alarmed, divided into three columns to attack Xiao Lun; he joined battle and routed them, beheading more than a thousand.

units.zh: 翌日，賊又來攻，相持日晚，賊稍引卻，南安侯駿以數十騎馳之。
units.en: The next day the rebels attacked again. The battle lasted until evening; as the rebels began to pull back, Marquis of Nan'an Jun charged them with several dozen horsemen.
units.literal: The next day the rebels attacked again. They fought until late in the day; the rebels gradually drew back. Marquis of Nan'an Jun charged them with several dozen horsemen.

units.zh: 賊回拒駿，駿部亂。
units.en: The rebels turned to meet Jun, and his unit broke ranks.
units.literal: The rebels turned to resist Jun, and Jun's detachment fell into disorder.

units.zh: 賊因逼大軍，軍遂潰。
units.en: The rebels pressed the main force, and the army collapsed.
units.literal: The rebels then pressed the main army, and the army collapsed.

units.zh: 綸至鐘山，衆裁千人，賊圍之，戰又敗，乃奔還京口。
units.en: Xiao Lun reached Zhongshan with barely a thousand men. The rebels besieged him; defeated again, he fled back to Jingkou.
units.literal: Xiao Lun reached Zhongshan with only about a thousand men. The rebels besieged him; he was defeated again and fled back to Jingkou.

units.zh: 三年春，綸復與東揚州刺史大連等入援，至于驃騎洲。
units.en: In spring of 549 Xiao Lun again marched to relieve the capital with Eastern Yangzhou regional inspector Dalian and others, reaching Piaoqi Isle.
units.literal: In spring of the third year, Xiao Lun again entered to relieve the capital together with Eastern Yangzhou Regional Inspector Dalian and others, reaching Piaoqi Isle.

units.zh: 進位司空。
units.en: He was promoted to minister of works.
units.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Works.

units.zh: 臺城陷，奔禹穴。
units.en: When the capital fell, he fled to the Yu Cave region.
units.literal: When the capital city fell, he fled to the Yu Cave region.

units.zh: 大寶元年，綸至郢州，刺史南平王恪讓州於綸，綸不受，乃上綸爲假黃鉞、都督中外諸軍事。
units.en: In 550 Xiao Lun reached Yingzhou. Regional inspector Prince of Nanping Ke offered him the province; Xiao Lun refused, so they elevated him as acting bearer of the yellow axe and area commander of all military affairs within and without.
units.literal: In the first year of Dabao, Xiao Lun reached Yingzhou. Regional Inspector Prince of Nanping Ke yielded the province to Xiao Lun; Xiao Lun did not accept, so they elevated Xiao Lun as Acting Bearer of the Yellow Axe and Area Commander of all military affairs within and without.

units.zh: 綸於是置百官，改廳事爲正陽殿。
units.en: Xiao Lun thereupon installed a full bureaucracy and renamed the office hall the Hall of Correct Yang.
units.literal: Xiao Lun thereupon established the full bureaucracy and renamed the office hall the Zhengyang Hall.

units.zh: 數有災怪，綸甚惡之。
units.en: Strange omens kept appearing, and Xiao Lun was deeply troubled by them.
units.literal: Omens and anomalies occurred repeatedly, and Xiao Lun deeply detested them.

units.zh: 時元帝圍河東王譽於長沙旣久，內外斷絕，綸聞其急，欲往救之，爲軍糧不繼，遂止。
units.en: At that time Emperor Yuan had long besieged Prince of Hedong Yu at Changsha, cutting the city off inside and out. When Xiao Lun heard how desperate the situation was, he wanted to go to his rescue, but with army provisions running short he had to abandon the plan.
units.literal: At that time Emperor Yuan had long besieged Prince of Hedong Yu at Changsha; inside and outside were cut off. When Xiao Lun heard of the emergency he wished to go rescue him, but because army provisions could not be maintained, he stopped.

units.zh: 乃與世祖書曰：
units.en: He then wrote to Emperor Yuan, saying:
units.literal: He then wrote to Emperor Yuan, saying:

units.zh: 伏以先朝聖德，孝治天下，九親雍睦，四表無怨，誠爲國政，實亦家風。
units.en: I reflect that our late emperor's sacred virtue ruled the realm through filial piety: the nine branches of kin lived in harmony, and no quarter of the empire nursed grievance. This was truly sound government—and it was our family's way.
units.literal: I reflect that the prior reign's sacred virtue governed the realm through filial piety; the nine kin were harmonious, and throughout the four quarters there was no resentment—truly the principle of statecraft, and indeed our family's tradition.

units.zh: 唯餘與爾，同奉神訓，宜敦旨喻，共承無改。
units.en: Only you and I remain to uphold our father's teaching. We ought to heed his words and together preserve what must not be changed.
units.literal: Only you and I remain to uphold the divine instruction; we ought to honor the edicts and join in preserving what must not be altered.

units.zh: 且道之斯美，以和爲貴，況天時地利，不及人和，豈可手足肱支，自相屠害。
units.en: The Way itself teaches that harmony is supreme—and when heaven's season and earth's advantage count for less than human accord, how can the arms and legs of one body turn on each other in slaughter?
units.literal: Moreover, in the beauty of the Way, harmony is prized; how much more when Heaven's season and Earth's advantage do not equal the harmony of men—how can limbs and joints of one body slaughter one another?

units.zh: 日者聞譽專情失訓，以幼陵長，湘、峽之內，遂至交鋒。
units.en: Lately I have heard that Yu, stubborn and heedless of instruction, let the young insult their elders, until fighting broke out across Xiang and the gorges.
units.literal: Recently I heard that Yu, fixated in his own will and failing in discipline, used youth to insult elders; within Xiang and Xia warfare broke out.

units.zh: 方等身遇亂兵，斃於行陣，殞于吳局。
units.en: Fangdeng ran into mutinous troops, was killed in battle, and died in the Wu campaign.
units.literal: Fangdeng encountered mutinous troops and fell in the battle line, perishing in the Wu affair.

units.zh: 方此非冤，聞問號怛，惟增摧憤，念以兼悼，當何可稱。
units.en: Even if his death was not unjust, the news made me cry out in grief; sorrow and rage only grew. When I think of this added loss, what words could be enough?
units.literal: At such a time, though this was no wrongful death, upon hearing the news I cried out in grief; sorrow and indignation only increased—when I think of this added grief, what words suffice?

units.zh: 吾在州所居遙隔，雖知其狀，未喻所然。
units.en: From my distant province I knew something of the situation, but not why it had come to this.
units.literal: While I was in my province, remote and distant, though I knew the situation I did not understand the reasons.

units.zh: 及屆此籓，備加覿訪，咸云譽應接多替，兵糧閉壅；
units.en: When I reached this princely domain and questioned everyone closely, all said Yu had been lax in receiving envoys and that military grain was blocked;
units.literal: When I arrived at this commandery and made thorough inquiries, all said Yu had been negligent in receiving envoys and that military grain transport was blocked;

units.zh: 弟教亦不悛，故興師以伐。
units.en: yet my younger brother's admonitions did not move him, and so troops were raised against him.
units.literal: yet my younger brother's admonitions also failed to make him reform; hence he raised troops to punish him.

units.zh: 譽未識大體，意斷所行，雖存急難，豈知竊思。
units.en: Yu failed to see the larger picture and acted on his own judgment alone. Though he was in grave danger, how could he know what others were thinking in private?
units.literal: Yu did not grasp the larger pattern and decided his course by personal whim; though he faced urgent peril, how could he know what others privately thought?

units.zh: 不能禮爭，復以兵來。
units.en: Unable to settle the matter through proper remonstrance, he answered with arms again.
units.literal: Unable to remonstrate through ritual propriety, he again came with troops.

units.zh: 蕭牆興變，體親成敵，一朝至此，能不鳴呼。
units.en: Disaster rose within our own walls; kin became enemies. When it has come to this in a single day, how can one not cry out?
units.literal: Trouble rose within the court walls; those bound by kinship became enemies—when it has come to this in a single morning, how can one not cry out?

units.zh: 旣有書問，雲雨傳流，噂栎遝其間，委悉無因詳究。
units.en: Letters have passed back and forth like clouds and rain, but slander and malice crowd between them, and I have had no way to learn the full truth.
units.literal: Though there have been letters back and forth like passing clouds and rain, slander and malice crowd between, and I have had no means to examine the details.

units.zh: 方今社稷危恥，創巨痛深，人非禽蟲，在知君父。
units.en: Now the altars of state stand in peril and shame; the wound is deep and the pain unbearable. Men are not birds or insects—they know their sovereign and their father.
units.literal: Now the altars of state are in peril and disgrace; wounds are deep and pain extreme. Men are not birds and insects—they know lord and father.

units.zh: 卽日大敵猶強，天仇未雪，余爾昆季，在外三人，如不匡難，安用臣子。
units.en: Even now the great enemy remains strong and heaven's vengeance is unrequited. Of us brothers, three are abroad—if we do not rescue the realm in its crisis, of what use are we as sons and subjects?
units.literal: Even today the great enemy remains strong and Heaven's vengeance is unsatisfied; of us brothers, three are abroad—if we do not rescue the crisis, of what use are we as ministers and sons?

units.zh: 唯應剖心嘗膽，泣血枕戈，感誓蒼穹，憑靈宗祀，晝謀夕計，共思匡復。
units.en: We should rend our hearts and taste gall, weep blood and sleep upon our spears, vow before heaven and invoke our ancestors, and plan day and night together to restore the realm.
units.literal: We should only rend our hearts and taste gall, weep blood and sleep upon our spears, vow before Heaven and invoke the imperial ancestors, planning day and night together to restore the realm.

units.zh: 至於其餘小忿，或宜寬貸。
units.en: As for lesser grievances, it may be right to show forbearance.
units.literal: As for other lesser resentments, it may be right to pardon them.

units.zh: 誠復子憾須臾，將奈國冤未逞。
units.en: A son's grievance may demand momentary satisfaction—but what of the nation's wrong, still unavenged?
units.literal: True, a son's grievance may demand momentary satisfaction—but what of the nation's wrong, still unrequited?

units.zh: 正當輕重相推，小大易奪，遣無益之情，割下流之悼，弘豁以理，通識勉之。
units.en: We ought to weigh the greater against the lesser, set aside what is small for what is large, release feelings that serve no purpose, and cut off lesser grief—with broad reason and shared understanding urging one another on.
units.literal: One ought to weigh the greater against the lesser, exchange the small for the large, send away feelings that profit nothing, cut off grief of lesser import, and with broad magnanimity and reason persuade one another through shared understanding.

units.zh: 今已喪鐘山，復誅猶子，將非揚湯止沸，吞冰療寒。
units.en: Zhongshan is already lost—must we also kill a nephew? Is that not like skimming boiling water or swallowing ice to cure a chill?
units.literal: Now that Zhongshan has already been lost, to kill a nephew as well—is this not like skimming boiling water or swallowing ice to cure a chill?

units.zh: 若以譽之無道，近遠同疾，弟復效尤，攸非獨罪。
units.en: If Yu's misconduct afflicts near and far alike, and my younger brother also follows his bad example, the fault is not Yu's alone.
units.literal: If because Yu is without the Way the near and far alike are afflicted, and my younger brother also follows his bad example, the fault is not Yu's alone.

units.zh: 幸寬於衆議，忍以事寧。
units.en: I beg you to yield to the consensus of many and bear with the situation until peace is restored.
units.literal: I hope you will yield to the consensus of many and bear with matters until peace is restored.

units.zh: 如使外寇未除，家禍仍構，料今訪古，未或弗亡。
units.en: If foreign enemies are not destroyed and domestic calamity continues, then whether I look to the present or search the past, no state has failed to perish.
units.literal: If outer bandits are not eliminated and domestic calamity still festers, whether I look at the present or examine the past, none have failed to perish.

units.zh: 夫征戰之理，義在克勝；
units.en: The principle of war lies in righteous victory over the enemy;
units.literal: The principle of campaign and battle lies in the righteousness of conquering the enemy;

units.zh: 至於骨肉之戰，愈勝愈酷，捷則非功，敗則有喪，勞兵損義，虧失多矣。
units.en: but in war among kin, the more one wins the crueler it grows. Victory brings no merit; defeat brings mourning. Troops are exhausted, righteousness is lost—the losses are many.
units.literal: Yet in warfare among kin, the more victory the more cruelty; if victorious there is no merit, if defeated there is mourning—the toil of troops and loss of righteousness, the losses are many.

units.zh: 侯景之軍所以未窺江外者，正爲籓屏盤固，宗鎮強密。
units.en: The reason Hou Jing's army has not yet looked beyond the Yangzi is precisely that the princely domains stand firm as a screen and the imperial fiefs are strong and secure.
units.literal: The reason Hou Jing's army has not yet peered beyond the Yangzi is precisely that the screen of princely domains stands firm and the imperial fiefs are strong and secure.

units.zh: 若自相魚肉，是代景行師。
units.en: If we devour one another, we fight Hou Jing's battles for him.
units.literal: If we devour one another like fish and flesh, we fight Hou Jing's battles for him.

units.zh: 景便不勞兵力，坐致成效，醜徒聞此，何快如之！
units.en: Hou Jing would need no effort of his own and would achieve his ends at leisure—how the vile rebel would rejoice at that!
units.literal: Hou Jing would exert no military effort yet achieve results at his ease—how the vile band would delight at this news!

units.zh: 又莊鐵小豎作亂，久挾觀寧、懷安二侯，以爲名號，當陽有事克掣，殊廢備境。
units.en: Moreover the petty rebel Zhuang Tie has risen in revolt, long holding the marquises of Guanning and Huai'an as his figureheads. Affairs at Dangyang had barely been settled when border defenses were wholly abandoned.
units.literal: Moreover the petty upstart Zhuang Tie rebelled, long holding hostage the two marquises Guanning and Huai'an as his banner; affairs at Dangyang had barely been checked when border defenses were wholly neglected.

units.zh: 第聞征伐，復致分兵，便是自於瓜州至於湘、雍，莫非戰地，悉以勞師。
units.en: On word of this campaign, troops were diverted again—so from Guazhou to Xiang and Yong, nowhere was free of battle, and every province exhausted its armies.
units.literal: Upon hearing of this campaign, troops were again diverted—thus from Guazhou to Xiang and Yong, nowhere was not a battlefield, all exhausting our armies.

units.zh: 侯景卒承虛藉釁，浮江豕突，豈不表裹成虞，首尾難救？
units.en: Hou Jing would then seize the opening, cross the Yangzi like a rampaging boar—would we not face danger within and without, impossible to save at either end?
units.literal: Hou Jing would then seize the void and exploit the opening, bursting across the Yangzi like a wild boar—would not danger arise within and without, head and tail impossible to save?

units.zh: 可爲寒心，其事已切。
units.en: It makes the blood run cold—and the matter is already urgent.
units.literal: One may well shudder at this—the matter is already urgent.

units.zh: 弟若苦陷洞庭，兵戈不戢，雍州疑迫，何以自安？
units.en: If my younger brother stubbornly presses the siege at Dongting and arms are not stilled, with Yongzhou under threat, how can he rest secure?
units.literal: If my younger brother stubbornly presses the siege at Dongting and arms are not stilled, with Yongzhou threatened and insecure, how can he rest easy?

units.zh: 必引進魏軍，以求形援。
units.en: He will inevitably invite Northern Wei troops to lend him force.
units.literal: He will inevitably invite Wei troops to seek physical support.

units.zh: 侯景事等內癰，西秦外同瘤腫。
units.en: Hou Jing is a carbuncle within; Western Qin is a tumor without.
units.literal: Hou Jing's affair is like a carbuncle within; Western Qin outwardly is like a tumorous swelling.

units.zh: 直置關中，已爲咽氣，況復貪狼難測，勢必侵吞。
units.en: Simply to place them at the passes would already choke our throat—how much more when greedy wolves are unpredictable and will surely invade and devour?
units.literal: Merely placing them at the passes would already choke the throat—how much more when greedy wolves are hard to fathom and will surely invade and swallow?

units.zh: 弟若不安，家國去矣。
units.en: If my younger brother is not secure, state and family are lost.
units.literal: If my younger brother is not secure, state and family are gone.

units.zh: 吾非有深鑒，獨能弘理，正是採藉風謠，博參物論，咸以爲疑，皆欲解體故耳。
units.en: I do not claim deep insight or unique wisdom—I am simply gathering what people say and consulting widely. All are troubled and wish only to withdraw.
units.literal: I do not have deep insight or alone can broadly apply reason—I am simply gathering prevailing rumors and widely consulting public opinion; all alike are troubled and wish only to withdraw.

units.zh: 自我國五十許年，恩格玄穹，德彌赤縣，雖有逆難，未亂邕熙。
units.en: In the fifty-odd years since our state was founded, grace has moved heaven and virtue filled the realm. Though there have been rebellions and crises, peace has not been overturned.
units.literal: Since our state was founded some fifty years, grace has moved Heaven and virtue filled the realm; though there have been rebellions and crises, tranquillity has not been overturned.

units.zh: 溥天率土，忠臣憤慨，比屋罹禍，忠義奮發，無不抱甲負戈，沖冠裂眥，咸欲剚刃於侯景腹中，所須兵主唱耳。
units.en: Under heaven and across the earth loyal ministers burn with outrage; every household suffers. Righteous fury flares—men don armor and take up weapons, bristling with rage, all wishing to drive blades into Hou Jing's belly. They need only a commander to lead them.
units.literal: Throughout heaven and earth loyal ministers burn with indignation; every household suffers disaster—righteous loyalty flares up, none failing to don armor and bear weapons, bristle with rage and split their eyes, all wishing to thrust blades into Hou Jing's belly—the need is only a commander to lead them.

units.zh: 今人皆樂死，赴者如流。
units.en: Now men are eager to die for the cause; volunteers come forward like a flowing stream.
units.literal: Now all men are willing to die; those who come forward are like a flowing stream.

units.zh: 弟英略振遠，雄伯當代，唯德唯藝，資文資武，拯溺濟難，朝野咸屬，一匡九合，非弟而誰？
units.en: My younger brother's heroic strategy resounds far and wide; you are the great leader of the age—in virtue and talent, in letters and arms, saving the drowning and relieving disaster. Court and country alike look to you to unite the realm—who but you?
units.literal: My younger brother's heroic strategy resounds afar; you are the great chieftain of the age—in virtue and skill, in literary and martial endowment, saving the drowning and relieving disaster, court and country alike look to you; to unite the realm in one effort—who but you?

units.zh: 豈得自違物望，致招羣讟！
units.en: How can you go against what the world expects and invite the censure of all!
units.literal: How can you go against the world's expectations and invite the censure of the multitude!

units.zh: 其間患難，具如所陳。
units.en: The hardships involved are as I have set forth.
units.literal: The hardships involved are as fully set forth as stated.

units.zh: 斯理皎然，無勞請箸；
units.en: This reasoning is clear and needs no further proof;
units.literal: This reasoning is clear and needs no further argument;

units.zh: 驗之以實，寧須確引。
units.en: tested against the facts, there is no need to cite examples at length.
units.literal: tested against the facts, there is no need to cite proof at length.

units.zh: 吾所以間關險道，出自東川，政謂上游諸籓，必連師狎至，庶以殘命，預在行間；
units.en: I crossed perilous routes from the eastern circuit because I believed the upper Yangzi princes would surely link their armies and arrive in succession, hoping with what life remains to take my place in the ranks;
units.literal: My reason for traversing perilous paths from the eastern circuit was precisely because I believed the upper Yangzi princely domains would surely link armies and arrive in succession, hoping with my remnant life to take part among the ranks;

units.zh: 及到九江，安北兄遂溯流更上，全由餼饋懸絕，卒食半菽，阻以菜色，無因進取。
units.en: When I reached Jiujiang, elder brother Anbei turned upstream again—entirely because supplies were cut off. We ate half beans at the end and were stopped by hunger, with no way to advance.
units.literal: When I reached Jiujiang, elder brother Anbei turned upstream and went farther upriver—entirely because provisions were cut off; we ate half beans at the end and were blocked by hunger, with no means to advance.

units.zh: 侯景方延假息，復緩誅刑，信增號憤，啓處無地。
units.en: Hou Jing was then buying time and deferring punishment—the news only deepened my cries of rage. I had nowhere to turn.
units.literal: Hou Jing was then prolonging a borrowed respite and deferring execution—indeed this only deepened my cries of rage; I had nowhere to stand or dwell.

units.zh: 計瀟湘穀粟，猶當紅委，若阻弟嚴兵，唯事交切，至於運轉，恐無暇發遣。
units.en: I reckon the grain of the Xiao-Xiang region is still abundant in store. If my younger brother's strict blockade continues, matters will only grow urgent—and as for transport, I fear there will be no time to dispatch it.
units.literal: I reckon the grain of the Xiao-Xiang region is still abundant in storage; if my younger brother's strict military blockade continues, matters will only grow urgent—as for transport, I fear there will be no leisure to dispatch it.

units.zh: 卽日萬心慊望，唯在民天，若遂等西河，時事殆矣。
units.en: Today every heart looks with eager hope only to grain, the people's heaven. If you persist as with the Xi River affair, the times will be nearly lost.
units.literal: Today ten thousand hearts look with eager hope only to the people's heaven; if you persist in equal treatment with the Xi River affair, the times will be nearly lost.

units.zh: 必希令弟豁照茲途，解汨川之圍，存社稷之計，使其運輸糧儲，應贍軍旅，庶協力一舉，指日寧泰。
units.en: I earnestly hope my younger brother will see this clearly, lift the siege on the Mil River, preserve the plan for the altars of state, and enable grain transport to supply the armies, so that with combined strength in one thrust peace may come within days.
units.literal: I earnestly hope my younger brother will open his eyes to this path, lift the siege on the Mil River, preserve the plan for the altars of state, and enable grain transport to supply the armies, so that with combined strength in one thrust peace may come within days.

units.zh: 宗廟重安，天下清復，推弟之功，豈非幸甚。
units.en: When the ancestral temples are secure again and the realm restored to order, to credit my younger brother's achievement—would that not be the greatest fortune?
units.literal: When the ancestral temples are again secure and the realm restored to order, to advance my younger brother's achievement—would that not be most fortunate?

units.zh: 吾才懦兵寡，安能爲役，所寄令弟，庶得申情，朝聞夕死，萬殞何恨。
units.en: My talent is weak and my troops few—I cannot serve in this cause. What I entrust to my younger brother is only that he may give voice to my feelings. If I hear his answer in the morning and die by evening, what regret in dying ten thousand deaths?
units.literal: My talent is weak and my troops few—I cannot serve as a tool in this; what I entrust to my younger brother is only that he may give voice to my feelings—hearing in the morning and dying at evening, what regret in dying ten thousand deaths?

units.zh: 聊陳聞見，幸無怪焉。
units.en: I have briefly set forth what I have heard and seen; I hope you will not take offense.
units.literal: I briefly set forth what I have heard and seen; I hope you will not take offense.

units.zh: 臨紙號迷，諸失次緒。
units.en: Facing the paper I cry out in confusion; my words fall out of order.
units.literal: Facing the paper I cry out in confusion; all is out of order.

units.zh: 世祖復書，陳河東有罪，不可解圍之狀。
units.en: Emperor Yuan wrote back, setting forth Prince of Hedong's crimes and explaining why the siege could not be lifted.
units.literal: Emperor Yuan replied in writing, setting forth Prince of Hedong's crimes and why the siege could not be lifted.

units.zh: 綸省書流涕曰：「天下之事，一至於斯！」
units.en: Reading the letter, Xiao Lun wept and said: "Affairs under heaven have come to this!"
units.literal: Reading the letter, Xiao Lun wept and said: "Affairs under Heaven have come to this!"

units.zh: 左右聞之，莫不掩泣。
units.en: His attendants, hearing this, all hid their faces and wept.
units.literal: Those around him, hearing this, none failed to cover their faces and weep.

units.zh: 於是大修器甲，將討侯景。
units.en: Thereupon he greatly refurbished armor and weapons, intending to campaign against Hou Jing.
units.literal: Thereupon he greatly refurbished armor and weapons, intending to campaign against Hou Jing.

units.zh: 元帝聞其強盛，乃遣王僧辯帥舟師一萬以逼綸，綸將劉龍武等降僧辯，綸軍潰，遂與子躓等十餘人輕舟走武昌。
units.en: When Emperor Yuan heard how strong he had become, he dispatched Wang Sengbian with ten thousand river troops to press Xiao Lun. Xiao Lun's general Liu Longwu and others surrendered to Wang Sengbian; Xiao Lun's army collapsed. He fled in a light boat to Wuchang with his son Zhi and more than ten others.
units.literal: When Emperor Yuan heard of his strength, he dispatched Wang Sengbian at the head of ten thousand river troops to press Xiao Lun. Xiao Lun's general Liu Longwu and others surrendered to Wang Sengbian; Xiao Lun's army collapsed. He then fled in a light boat to Wuchang with his son Zhi and more than ten others.

units.zh: 時綸長史韋質、司馬薑律先在于外，聞綸敗，馳往迎之。
units.en: At that time Xiao Lun's chief clerk Wei Zhi and marshal Jiang Lu were already abroad; hearing of his defeat they raced to meet him.
units.literal: At that time Xiao Lun's chief clerk Wei Zhi and marshal Jiang Lu were already abroad; hearing of Xiao Lun's defeat they raced to meet him.

units.zh: 於是復收散卒，屯于齊昌郡，將引魏軍共攻南陽。
units.en: Thereupon he gathered scattered troops again and encamped in Qichang commandery, intending to bring in Northern Wei troops to attack Nanyang jointly.
units.literal: Thereupon he again gathered scattered troops and encamped in Qichang commandery, intending to lead Wei troops jointly to attack Nanyang.

units.zh: 侯景將任約聞之，使鐵騎二百襲綸，綸無備，又敗走定州。
units.en: Hou Jing's general Ren Yue heard of this and sent two hundred armored horsemen to raid Xiao Lun. Unprepared, Xiao Lun was defeated again and fled to Dingzhou.
units.literal: Hou Jing's general Ren Yue heard of this and sent two hundred iron cavalry to raid Xiao Lun; unprepared, Xiao Lun was again defeated and fled to Dingzhou.

units.zh: 定州刺史田龍祖迎綸，綸以龍祖荊鎮所任，懼爲所執，復歸齊昌。
units.en: Dingzhou regional inspector Tian Longzu welcomed Xiao Lun, but Xiao Lun, knowing Longzu had been appointed from the Jing garrison, feared being seized and returned to Qichang.
units.literal: Dingzhou Regional Inspector Tian Longzu welcomed Xiao Lun; Xiao Lun, because Longzu had been appointed from the Jing circuit garrison, feared being seized and returned to Qichang.

units.zh: 行至汝南，西魏所署汝南城主李素者，綸之故吏，聞綸敗，開城納之。
units.en: When he reached Runan, Li Su—commandant of Runan appointed by Western Wei and Xiao Lun's former subordinate—hearing of his defeat, opened the city and received him.
units.literal: When he reached Runan, Li Su—commandant of Runan city appointed by Western Wei and Xiao Lun's former clerk—hearing of Xiao Lun's defeat, opened the city and received him.

units.zh: 綸乃脩浚城池，收集士卒，將攻竟陵。
units.en: Xiao Lun then repaired the walls and moat, gathered troops, and prepared to attack Jingling.
units.literal: Xiao Lun then repaired and dredged the walls and moat, gathered soldiers, and intended to attack Jingling.

units.zh: 西魏安州刺史馬岫聞之，報于西魏，西魏遣大將軍楊忠、儀同侯幾通率衆赴焉。
units.en: Ma Xiu, regional inspector of Anzhou under Western Wei, heard of this and reported to his court. Western Wei sent Grand General Yang Zhong and Yitong Hou Jitong with an army to intervene.
units.literal: Ma Xiu, Regional Inspector of Anzhou under Western Wei, heard of this and reported to Western Wei. Western Wei sent Grand General Yang Zhong and Yitong Hou Jitong to lead troops there.

units.zh: 二年二月，忠等至于汝南，綸嬰城自守。
units.en: In the second month of 551, Yang Zhong and his force reached Runan. Xiao Lun shut the gates and held the city.
units.literal: In the second month of the second year, Zhong and the others reached Runan. Xiao Lun closed the city and defended himself.

units.zh: 會天寒大雪，忠等攻不能克，死者甚衆。
units.en: Bitter cold and heavy snow set in; Yang Zhong could not storm the city, and his losses were very heavy.
units.literal: It happened that the weather turned bitterly cold with heavy snow. Zhong and the others could not take the city by assault, and very many died.

units.zh: 後李素中流矢卒，城乃陷。
units.en: Later Li Su was killed by a stray arrow, and the city fell.
units.literal: Later Li Su was struck by a stray arrow and died, and the city then fell.

units.zh: 忠等執綸，綸不爲屈，遂害之。
units.en: Yang Zhong seized Xiao Lun. He refused to yield and was put to death.
units.literal: Zhong and the others seized Xiao Lun. He would not submit and was thereupon killed.

units.zh: 投于江岸，經日顏色不變，鳥獸莫敢近焉。
units.en: His body was thrown on the riverbank. For a full day his face did not change, and neither bird nor beast dared come near.
units.literal: His body was cast on the riverbank. For a whole day his complexion did not change, and birds and beasts did not dare approach.

units.zh: 時年三十三。
units.en: He was thirty-three.
units.literal: He was then thirty-three years old.

units.zh: 百姓憐之，爲立祠廟，後世祖追諡曰攜。
units.en: The people pitied him and erected a shrine in his honor. Later Emperor Yuan posthumously titled him Xie.
units.literal: The common people pitied him and built a shrine for him. Later Emperor Yuan posthumously gave him the title Xie.

units.zh: 長子堅，字長白。
units.en: His eldest son Jian, styled Changbai.
units.literal: His eldest son was Jian, styled Changbai.

units.zh: 大同元年，以例封汝南侯，邑五百戶。
units.en: In 535, by precedent he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Runan with a fief of five hundred households.
units.literal: In the first year of Datong, by precedent he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Runan with a fief of five hundred households.

units.zh: 亦善草隸，性頗庸短。
units.en: He was also skilled in cursive and clerical script, but by nature he was rather dull and limited.
units.literal: He also excelled at cursive and clerical script, but his nature was rather mediocre and limited.

units.zh: 侯景圍城，堅屯太陽門，終日蒲飲，不撫軍政。
units.en: When Hou Jing besieged the capital, Jian held the Taiyang Gate, drinking all day on rush mats and neglecting military affairs.
units.literal: When Hou Jing besieged the city, Jian held the Taiyang Gate, drinking all day on rush mats and not attending to military affairs.

units.zh: 吏士有功，未嘗申理，疫癘所加，亦不存卹，士咸憤怨。
units.en: He never reported the deeds of deserving officers and men. When plague struck, he offered no relief. The troops were furious.
units.literal: When officers and soldiers had merit, he never reported it. When plague struck, he showed no care or relief. The troops were all angry and resentful.

units.zh: 太清三年三月，堅書佐董勛華、白曇朗等以繩引賊登樓，城遂陷，堅遇害。
units.en: In the third month of 549, Jian's clerks Dong Xunhua, Bai Tanlang, and others used ropes to let the rebels scale the walls. The city fell, and Jian was killed.
units.literal: In the third month of the third year of Taiqing, Jian's clerical assistants Dong Xunhua, Bai Tanlang, and others used ropes to let the bandits climb the tower. The city then fell, and Jian was killed.

units.zh: 弟確，字仲正。
units.en: His younger brother Que, styled Zhongzheng.
units.literal: His younger brother was Que, styled Zhongzheng.

units.zh: 少驍勇，有文才。
units.en: As a youth he was bold and brave and had literary talent.
units.literal: In youth he was valiant and brave and had literary talent.

units.zh: 大同二年，封爲正階侯，邑五百戶，後徙封永安。
units.en: In 536 he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhengjie with five hundred households, and later transferred to the title Marquis of Yong'an.
units.literal: In the second year of Datong he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhengjie with a fief of five hundred households, and later was transferred to the enfeoffment of Yong'an.

units.zh: 常在第中習騎射，學兵法，時人皆以爲狂。
units.en: He constantly practiced mounted archery at home and studied military tactics. People at the time thought him mad.
units.literal: He constantly practiced mounted archery in his residence and studied military tactics. People of the time all thought him mad.

units.zh: 左右或以進諫，確曰：「聽吾爲國家破賊，使汝知之。」
units.en: His attendants sometimes tried to dissuade him. Que said, "Wait until I break the rebels for the state—then you will see."
units.literal: Those at his side sometimes offered remonstrance. Que said, "Wait until I break the bandits for the state—then you will know."

units.zh: 除秘書丞，太子中舍人。
units.en: He was appointed assistant in the Secretariat and attendant in the heir apparent's household.
units.literal: He was appointed Assistant in the Secretariat and Attendant of the Heir Apparent's Household.

units.zh: 鐘山之役，確苦戰，所向披靡，羣虜憚之。
units.en: At the battle on Zhongshan, Que fought fiercely, routing every foe he met; the rebels all feared him.
units.literal: In the battle at Zhongshan, Que fought bitterly. Wherever he turned, the enemy was swept away, and the bandits all feared him.

units.zh: 確每臨陣對敵，意氣詳贍。
units.en: Whenever Que faced the enemy in battle, his bearing was calm and confident.
units.literal: Whenever Que faced the enemy in battle, his spirit was composed and ample.

units.zh: 帶甲據鞍，自朝及夕，馳驟往反，不以爲勞，諸將服其壯勇。
units.en: Armored and in the saddle from dawn to dusk, he rode back and forth without tiring. The generals admired his courage.
units.literal: Armored and in the saddle from morning to evening, he galloped back and forth and did not count it labor. The generals admired his bold courage.

units.zh: 及侯景乞盟，確在外，慮爲後患，啓求召確入城。
units.en: When Hou Jing sued for peace, Que was outside the walls. Fearing he would become a threat later, a memorial asked that Que be recalled into the city.
units.literal: When Hou Jing begged for a truce, Que was outside the city. Fearing he would become a future threat, someone memorialized asking that Que be summoned into the city.

units.zh: 詔乃召確爲南中郎將、廣州刺史，增封二千戶。
units.en: An edict summoned Que as General of the Southern Gentlemen and regional inspector of Guangzhou, with an added fief of two thousand households.
units.literal: An edict then summoned Que as General of the Southern Gentlemen and Regional Inspector of Guangzhou, with an added fief of two thousand households.

units.zh: 確知此盟多貳，城必淪沒，因欲南奔。
units.en: Que knew the truce was treacherous and the city would fall, and he wanted to flee south.
units.literal: Que knew this truce was full of treachery and that the city would surely be lost, and therefore wished to flee south.

units.zh: 攜王聞之，逼確使入，確猶不肯。
units.en: Prince Yo heard of this and pressed Que to enter, but Que still refused.
units.literal: Prince Yo heard of this and forced Que to enter, but Que still would not agree.

units.zh: 攜王流涕謂曰：「汝欲反邪！」
units.en: Prince Yo wept and said, "Are you trying to rebel?"
units.literal: Prince Yo wept and said, "Do you wish to rebel?"

units.zh: 時臺使周石珍在坐，確謂石珍曰：「侯景雖云欲去，而不解長圍，以意而推，其事可見。
units.en: The court envoy Zhou Shizhen was present. Que told him, "Hou Jing says he will leave, but he keeps the long siege intact. That tells you what he really intends.
units.literal: At that time the capital envoy Zhou Shizhen was present. Que said to Shizhen, "Although Hou Jing says he wishes to leave, he does not lift the long siege. Reasoning from this, his intent is clear.

units.zh: 今召我入，未見其益也。」
units.en: Summoning me inside now will do no good."
units.literal: Now summoning me in, I see no benefit in it."

units.zh: 石珍曰：「敕旨如此，侯豈得辭？」
units.en: Shizhen said, "That is the emperor's order. How can you refuse?"
units.literal: Shizhen said, "The imperial command is thus. How can the marquis decline?"

units.zh: 確執意猶堅，攜王大怒，謂趙伯超曰：「譙州，卿爲我斬之，當賚首赴闕。」
units.en: Que would not budge. Prince Xie flew into a rage and told Zhao Bochao, "Qiaozhou, cut him down for me and bring his head to the court."
units.literal: Que's resolve was still firm. Prince Xie was greatly angered and said to Zhao Bochao, "Qiaozhou, cut him down for me and bring his head to the court."

units.zh: 伯超揮刃眄確曰：「我識君耳，刀豈識君？」
units.en: Bochao drew his blade and looked at Que. "I know you," he said, "but does my blade?"
units.literal: Bochao brandished his blade and glanced at Que, saying, "I know you—but does my blade know you?"

units.zh: 確於是流涕而出，遂入城。
units.en: Que wept as he left, then entered the city.
units.literal: Que thereupon wept as he went out and then entered the city.

units.zh: 及景背盟復圍城，城陷，確排闥入，啓高祖曰：「城已陷矣。」
units.en: When Hou Jing broke the truce and besieged the city again, the walls fell. Que burst through the inner gate and told Emperor Wu, "The city is lost."
units.literal: When Jing broke the truce and again besieged the city, the city fell. Que pushed open the inner gate and reported to Gaozu, "The city has fallen."

units.zh: 高祖曰：「猶可一戰不？」
units.en: Emperor Wu asked, "Can we still fight one more battle?"
units.literal: Gaozu said, "Can we still fight one battle?"

units.zh: 對曰：「不可。
units.en: He answered, "No.
units.literal: He answered, "We cannot.

units.zh: 臣向者親格戰，勢不能禁，自縋下城，僅得至此。」
units.en: I was fighting hand to hand and could not hold them. I let myself down from the wall on a rope and barely made it here."
units.literal: Your subject just now fought hand to hand and could not hold them back. I lowered myself by rope from the wall and barely reached here."

units.zh: 高祖歎曰：「自我得之，自我失之，亦復何恨。」
units.en: Emperor Wu sighed and said, "I won it myself and I lose it myself—what is there to regret?"
units.literal: Gaozu sighed and said, "I gained it myself and I lose it myself—what regret is there?"

units.zh: 乃使確爲慰勞文。
units.en: He then had Que draft a letter of consolation to the troops.
units.literal: He then had Que draft a letter of consolation.

units.zh: 確旣出見景，景愛其膂力，恒令在左右。
units.en: When Que went out to see Hou Jing, Hou Jing admired his strength and always kept him close.
units.literal: When Que went out and saw Jing, Jing admired his physical strength and always kept him at his side.

units.zh: 後從景行，見天上飛鳶，羣虜爭射不中，確射之，應弦而落。
units.en: Later, marching with Hou Jing, they saw a kite overhead. The rebels all shot and missed. Que shot once and brought it down.
units.literal: Later, following Jing on the march, they saw a kite flying in the sky. The bandits all shot at it but missed. Que shot it, and it fell at the twang of the bowstring.

units.zh: 賊徒忿嫉，咸勸除之。
units.en: The rebels were jealous and urged that he be killed.
units.literal: The bandits were resentful and jealous, and all urged that he be eliminated.

units.zh: 先是攜王遣人密導確，確謂使者曰：「侯景輕佻，可一夫力致，確不惜死，正欲手刃之；
units.en: Earlier Prince Yo had sent a secret envoy to Que. Que told him, "Hou Jing is reckless and could be brought down by one man. I do not fear death—I mean to kill him with my own hand;
units.literal: Earlier Prince Yo had sent someone in secret to guide Que. Que told the envoy, "Hou Jing is frivolous and can be brought down by one man's strength. I do not spare my life and mean to kill him with my own hand;

units.zh: 但未得其便耳。
units.en: I only lack the chance.
units.literal: only I have not yet found the opportunity.

units.zh: 卿還啓家王，願勿以爲念也。」
units.en: Go back and tell my father not to worry about me."
units.literal: When you return, report to my prince and ask that he not worry on my account."

units.zh: 事未遂而爲賊所害。
units.en: Before he could act, the rebels killed him.
units.literal: The affair did not succeed, and he was killed by the bandits.

units.zh: 史臣曰：自周、漢廣樹籓屏，固本深根；
units.en: The historian remarks: From Zhou and Han onward, feudal princes were widely enfeoffed to secure the dynasty at its roots;
units.literal: The historian says: From Zhou and Han, feudal screens were widely planted to strengthen the root deep in the soil;

units.zh: 高祖之封建，將遵古制也。
units.en: Emperor Wu's enfeoffments were meant to follow that ancient model.
units.literal: Gaozu's enfeoffments were intended to follow the ancient system.

units.zh: 南康、廬陵並以宗室之貴，據磐石之重，績以孝著，續以勇聞。
units.en: Nankang and Luling, as members of the imperial house, held the weight of bedrock posts. Ji was known for filial piety, Xu for courage.
units.literal: Nankang and Luling both, by the honor of the imperial clan, held the weight of bedrock. Ji was noted for filial piety, Xu for courage.

units.zh: 綸聰警有才學，性險躁，屢以罪黜，及太清之亂，忠孝獨存，斯可嘉矣。
units.en: Lun was clever and learned, but rash and volatile; he was repeatedly punished for offenses. Yet amid the Taiqing turmoil he alone kept faith and filial duty—this is praiseworthy.
units.literal: Lun was clever and alert, with talent and learning, but his nature was dangerous and restless. Repeatedly he was dismissed for offenses. Yet in the chaos of Taiqing, loyalty and filial piety alone remained in him—this is worthy of praise.

units.zh: 己酉，周將楊忠帥突厥阿史那木汗等二十餘萬人自恒州分為三道，殺掠吏人。
units.en: On the jiyou day, the Northern Zhou general Yang Zhong led more than two hundred thousand men, including the Turk Ashina Muhan, from Heng Province in three columns, killing and plundering officials and commoners.
units.literal: On the jiyou day, Zhou general Yang Zhong led more than two hundred thousand men including the Turk Ashina Muhan from Heng Province in three columns, killing and plundering officials and commoners.

units.zh: 生世子方等、益昌公主含貞。
units.en: She bore the heir Fangdeng and Princess Yichang Hanzhen.
units.literal: She bore the heir Fangdeng and Princess Yichang Hanzhen.

units.zh: 太宗簡文皇帝諱綱，字世纘，小字六通，高祖第三子，昭明太子母弟也。
units.en: Taizong Emperor Jianwen, personal name Gang, courtesy name Shizuan, childhood name Liutong, was Gaozu's third son and Zhaoming Crown Prince's younger brother by the same mother.
units.literal: The Taizong Emperor Jianwen was tabooed Gang, style name Shizuan, childhood name Liutong; he was the third son of the Gaozu and a uterine younger brother of Crown Prince Zhaoming.

units.zh: 三年四月乙巳，昭明太子薨。
units.en: On yisi in the fourth month of year 3 Crown Prince Zhaoming died.
units.literal: In the fourth month, day yisi, year 3, Crown Prince Zhaoming died.

units.zh: 所著《昭明太子傳》五卷，《諸王傳》三十卷，《禮大義》二十卷，《老子義》二十卷，《莊子義》二十卷，《長春義記》一百卷，《法寶連璧》三百卷，並行於世焉。
